topic: The Visual Heart of Linear Algebra: Understanding Vectors
target_audience: First-year university students or advanced high school students interested in STEM

sections.title: Prerequisite: From Points to Directions
lecture_lines: A point represents a static location in space.
A vector is different; it represents movement.
Think of it as a journey, not a destination.
animations: Show a #FFFFFF point at (0,0) labeled 'Location'.
Draw a #FFD700 vector arrow starting from the #FFFFFF point.
Animate a #00FF00 dot traveling along the #FFD700 vector.

sections.title: The Geometry of a Vector
lecture_lines: Visually, we represent a vector as an arrow.
Every vector has a specific length, called magnitude.
Every vector also points in a specific direction.
You can slide a vector anywhere on the grid.
It remains the same if magnitude and direction persist.
animations: Draw a #00FFFF arrow labeled 'Vector' in the center.
Highlight the #00FFFF arrow's length and label it 'Magnitude'.
Flash the #00FFFF arrow's tip and label its angle 'Direction'.
Shift the #00FFFF arrow to a new grid position.
Pulse the #00FFFF arrow to show it is unchanged.

sections.title: The Algebra of Vectors: The 'Recipe'
lecture_lines: We write vectors as a list of numbers.
The numbers act as a recipe for movement.
Component x moves right; component y moves up.
animations: Display a #FFFFFF column matrix [4, 1] on the side, accompanied by [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/recipe.svg].
Trace a dashed #FFFFFF path 4 units right from origin.
Draw the resulting #FF4500 vector arrow over the path.

sections.title: Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Method
lecture_lines: Adding vectors is like following sequential instructions.
Place the second vector's tail at the first's tip.
The result is the arrow from start to end.
Numerically, we simply add the corresponding components.
This new vector represents the combined total movement.
animations: Draw a #1E90FF vector labeled 'A' starting from origin.
Place a #FF00FF vector 'B' at 'A's tip.
Draw a #FFFF00 vector from origin to 'B's tip.
Display addition: [x1+x2, y1+y2] in #FFFFFF near the vectors.
Flash the #FFFF00 resultant vector to show total movement.

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication: Scaling the World
lecture_lines: Scalars are regular numbers that scale our vectors.
Multiplying by a scalar stretches or shrinks the arrow.
A scalar of two doubles the vector's length.
Negative scalars flip the vector to the opposite direction.
This scaling is the core of linear transformations.
animations: Show a #ADFF2F vector 'v' and scalar 'k' positioned over the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/world.svg] icon.
Animate the #ADFF2F vector changing length based on 'k'.
Scale the #ADFF2F vector to exactly twice its length.
Flip the #ADFF2F vector to point in the opposite direction.
Pulse the scaled #ADFF2F vector to emphasize the transformation.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
lecture_lines: Vectors are both geometric arrows and numerical lists.
They power physics engines, graphics, and data science.
Mastering vectors unlocks the heart of linear algebra.
animations: Show a #FFFFFF arrow alongside its #FFFFFF [x, y] matrix.
Display a #00FF00 grid of arrows representing a force field, incorporating the physics icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/physics.svg].
Scale the #00FF00 grid to show a linear transformation.
